The ratio is the sex's average ANA divided by the mean of the per-sex average ANA values (an unweighted mean across sexes).
Same as 1, but the denominator is the overall average of the per-patient ANA values across all matched patients (a patient-weighted mean), not the mean of the per-sex averages.
Same as 1, but the ratio is computed only for sexes with non-null `SEX`, so patients with missing `SEX` are dropped and do not form a group.
Same as 1, but patients with missing `SEX` form their own group (NULL or empty), and that group is included in the mean of the per-sex ANA averages.
Same as 1, but the sex groups include only those with at least one non-null `ANA` value. The denominator mean is taken over those groups only.
Same as 1, but a patient with a null `aCL IgG` or null `ANA` across all examinations is excluded from both averages. This means both averages cover the same set of patients.
Same as 1, but each average ignores nulls independently. The `aCL IgG` average covers patients with a non-null `aCL IgG`, and the `ANA` average covers patients with a non-null `ANA`.
The per-patient average is taken over examination records with non-null values only. A patient whose values are all null contributes nothing to that average.
The output is one row per sex with four columns: sex, average `aCL IgG`, average `ANA`, and the ANA ratio.
The ratio is a relative ANA index: values above 1 mean the sex's average ANA is above the cross-sex mean, and values below 1 mean it is below.
Patients are matched to examinations through `Examination.ID = Patient.ID` using an inner join. Examinations with no matching patient are dropped, and patients with no examinations do not appear.
`SEX` values are grouped as stored (for example 'F', 'M'), with no normalization of case or whitespace.
The ratio's denominator is the mean of the per-sex average ANA values, with each sex weighted equally, even if the sexes have very different patient counts.
The numbers are not rounded and are returned at full floating-point precision.
queries:
WITH p AS (
  SELECT P.SEX AS SEX, E.ID AS ID, AVG(E.`aCL IgG`) AS g, AVG(E.ANA) AS a
  FROM Examination E
  JOIN Patient P ON P.ID = E.ID
  GROUP BY E.ID, P.SEX
),
s AS (
  SELECT SEX, AVG(g) AS avg_igg, AVG(a) AS avg_ana
  FROM p
  GROUP BY SEX
)
SELECT SEX, avg_igg, avg_ana, avg_ana / (SELECT AVG(avg_ana) FROM s) AS ratio
FROM s
WITH p AS (
    SELECT P.ID, P.SEX, AVG(E.ANA) AS a
    FROM Patient P
    JOIN Examination E ON E.ID = P.ID
    WHERE E.ANA IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY P.ID, P.SEX
)
SELECT SEX, AVG(a) / (SELECT AVG(a) FROM p) AS ratio
FROM p
GROUP BY SEX;
SELECT SEX, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM Patient WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL) AS ratio
FROM Patient
WHERE SEX IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY SEX;
SELECT AVG(avg_ana)
FROM (
    SELECT AVG(e.ANA) AS avg_ana
    FROM Examination e
    JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
    GROUP BY COALESCE(NULLIF(p.SEX, ''), '')
);
SELECT AVG(`aCL IgG`), AVG(ANA)
FROM Examination
WHERE ID IN (
    SELECT ID
    FROM Examination
    GROUP BY ID
    HAVING COUNT(`aCL IgG`) > 0 AND COUNT(ANA) > 0
);
